prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi statue portrait. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman in dark vampire makeup — pale porcelain skin, deep burgundy-black shadow smudged heavily beneath both eyes, sharp black liner, long dramatic lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a glossy near-black wine lip, sharply contoured cheekbones, long straight jet-black hair, a cold, poised expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a thick black-steel bar and a pointed silver stud.

Piercings: A thin gold septum ring hangs below the nose with a smaller ring above it, and a gold ring passes through each nostril; two thin gold bars pass through the outer end of each eyebrow; a gold Medusa stud sits above the lips; a gold hoop passes through the lower lip's edge with a snake-bite ring on each side and one small ring beside it; a gold labret stud and one ring pass through the chin; one small gold stud sits on each jaw; on each ear four oversized pieces — a huge gold hoop hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder, a wide ear cuff, a large pearl drop and a helix ring. All jewelry is real gold, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest, a cinched waist above a big soft rounded belly and enormous round hips, thick soft thighs disappearing out of the bottom of the frame.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips and both distinct thighs — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of genuine purpleheart wood, a striking deep violet-purple heartwood, unmistakably not a human skin tone, with fine straight grain lines running through it and a few darker plum-coloured streaks, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same wood. A little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, each thigh individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, deeply polished tip — the two thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — no knees, no calves, no feet, nothing continues below either tip — the material simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque carved wood — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same dense solidity throughout, catching light only as reflections on its polished surface, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep violet on one side and a cool silver on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so a deep violet glances off the left half and a cool silver glances off the right half. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
